gaps: No pciIds on any record. Intel/AMD PCI device ids were not emitted because I am not confident enough in specific hex ids to risk poisoning the alias resolver; scripts/parse-aliases.ts harvests them from pci.ids anyway.
No Arc B770 or any Battlemage part above B580. I could not confirm such a desktop SKU actually shipped, and the BRIEF says omit rather than invent.
No Arc Pro workstation cards (A40/A50/A60, Pro B50/B60) — professional SKUs, and I am not confident of their full specs.
No Intel Iris Xe MAX (DG1). It was an OEM-only discrete part and I am not confident of its retail desktop presence or clocks.
No Panther Lake / Xe3 integrated graphics. I cannot confirm the shipping SKU names or clocks, so the newest Intel iGPU generation is missing.
baseClockMHz is null on every record. Intel publishes no base clock for Arc; iGPU graphics base frequency varies per host CPU SKU and I did not want to pick one arbitrarily.
recommendedPsuW populated only for A750/A770 (Intel states 600W). Null for A310/A380/A580/B570/B580.

lengthMm/slotWidth/powerConnectors populated only where an Intel reference/Limited Edition design exists (A750, A770 16GB, B580). A380/A310/A580/B570 are AIB-only designs with wide variance, so those fields are null.
driverEolDate is null on every record, including the eol Gen6-Gen8 Intel parts — I know support ended but not the exact dates.
fp32TFLOPS is null for HD Graphics 2000/3000 (Gen6). Sandy Bridge EUs have no FMA, so shaders*clock*2 overstates them by 2x and emitting it would have been a knowingly wrong number.
Desktop Ryzen 8500G/8600G iGPU clocks (740M/760M at desktop power) not emitted as separate records; only the mobile Phoenix clocks are covered, plus the 8700G 780M which I am confident about.
Mobile-only Vega APU configurations (4800U/5800U-class Vega 8 at their own clocks) are not covered; only desktop APU parts.
No Intel Iris Plus 640/650/655 (Kaby Lake-R/Coffee Lake GT3e) and no UHD P630 workstation part.
No Meteor Lake-U 4 Xe-core "Intel Graphics" record — I was not confident enough in its max frequency.
uncertainties: FIELD SEMANTICS DEVIATION: `shaders` holds ALU/shading-unit counts for Intel, NOT EU counts (EU x 8 for Gen6-Gen12 Xe-LP; Xe-core x 128 for Xe-HPG/Xe-LPG/Xe2). Using EU counts would make fp32TFLOPS fail the BRIEF consistency rule by 8x and make Intel shader counts non-comparable with AMD/Nvidia. EU counts are recoverable: shaders/8 for pre-Arc, shaders/128 = Xe-cores for Arc.
Intel ALUs are still not perf-equivalent to AMD stream processors or Nvidia CUDA cores at equal count and clock; any fit that uses `shaders` across vendors needs a per-architecture efficiency term.

iGPU boostClockMHz is a per-CPU-SKU figure, not a property of the graphics name. I used a representative flagship host SKU for each (e.g. UHD 770 Alder Lake = i9-12900K 1550 MHz, Raptor Lake = i9-13900K 1650 MHz, HD 530 = i7-6700K 1150 MHz). Lower-tier hosts with the same graphics name run several hundred MHz lower.

Arc A770 boost is Intel published "Graphics Clock" 2100 MHz; third-party databases commonly list 2400 MHz peak, which would give ~19.7 TFLOPS instead of 17.2. My triple is internally consistent at 2100.

Least confident clocks: UHD 600 (700 MHz), UHD 605 (750 MHz), HD 510 (1000 MHz), Iris Graphics 540 (1050 MHz), Iris Plus G4 (1050 MHz), Arrow Lake-S iGPU (2000 MHz), Arc 130V (1850 MHz), Meteor Lake 7 Xe-core (2200 MHz), Vega 6 Cezanne (1700 MHz).
Arc 140V is 1950 MHz on Core Ultra 7 258V but runs higher (~2050 MHz) on the Core Ultra 9 288V; I used 1950.

shaderModel 6_0 assigned to all pre-Xe DX12 Intel parts (Gen9/9.5/11). Real driver-exposed SM may be higher (6.4-6.5) on Gen11; I under-claimed deliberately, which could produce false SHADER_MODEL gate failures on those parts.

upscaling lists mark XeSS on Xe-LP via the DP4a path, and FSR on any DX12-class part since FSR is shader-based. If `upscaling` is meant strictly as "vendor-hardware-accelerated path", the FSR entries on Intel parts should be dropped.

AMD driverStatus for Vega APU graphics set to legacy per the BRIEF rule for GCN 4/5. In practice Cezanne/Renoir Vega still receives Adrenalin updates, so maintenance may be the better label for those four records.
A580 is 1700 MHz / 24 Xe-cores per Intel; it is the SKU I am least sure of among Alchemist because it launched quietly a year after the rest.

RDNA 3/3.5 fp32TFLOPS uses the single-issue convention (shaders * clock * 2). AMD marketing figures for 780M/890M are 2x these because they count dual-issue FP32. The AMD dGPU agent must use the same convention or the two catalogues will not be comparable.
Radeon 8060S (Strix Halo) launch is given as 2025-01 (CES announcement); retail systems shipped somewhat later.
